edits.old: Six other Halomonas genomes also contained multiple MPn transport and degradation genes, while 17 did not (Figure 5).
edits.new: In GTDB release R232, which divides the former genus *Halomonas* among *Halomonas*, *Vreelandella*, and several smaller genera, both isolates remain in *Halomonas*: *H. saccharevitans* shares 98.5% average nucleotide identity (ANI) with the type strain genome, and *Halomonas* sp. D is the representative of its own species cluster (*Halomonas* sp032334135; closest other species, 92.7% ANI). Six other reference genomes labeled *Halomonas* also contained multiple MPn transport and degradation genes, while 17 did not (Figure 5); in GTDB R232, three of these six (*Halomonas* sp. PBN3, *H. huangheensis*, and *Halomonas* sp. S2151) remain in *Halomonas*, whereas *H. jeotgali* is now placed in *Vreelandella* and *H. zincidurans* and *H. lutea* in *Modicisalibacter*.
edits.rationale: Reports the isolates' R232 placement (review comment 3). The six/17 counts still describe the Figure 5 labels, but three of the six MPn-positive 'Halomonas' references are in other genera in R232. All six are resolved unambiguously by strain, so this sentence does not depend on the H. campaniensis inference. I1's GTDB match is to its own deposited genome, so it is described as its own species cluster, not as a 100% ANI identification.

edits.old: only Halomonas contains members with the genes encoding the C-P lyase pathway
edits.new: This is a genus-level statement based on reference genomes (Figure 5). In the metagenome, neither Halomonadaceae MAG carries C–P lyase genes (phnF–P, including phnJ): Halomonas.1 (H. fontilapidosi) and 2020 Halomonas.2 (now Vreelandella.1 in R232). Neither isolate matches any of the 450 MAGs at species level (skani: best pair I4 vs Halomonas.1, 85.7% ANI over ~25% of the genome). The C-P lyase Halomonas is therefore supported by the isolate, not by the MAGs; consider saying so where Halomonas is presented as the case study (the Culturing discussion and the Conclusions).

edits.old: The values were further normalized by DNA measurements to control for variability in biomass density among the samples.   Pearson coefficients were calculated between these two sets of methane concentrations, and linear equations of the line-of-best-fit from these correlations were reported.
edits.new: Because each model’s biomass had been fixed to its relative abundance divided by the DNA concentration of each depth, the simulated methane flux of each methylphosphonate-consuming member was rescaled to the member’s biomass in each core (its relative abundance times the soil DNA concentration of each depth, weighted by the depth intervals of 5 and 10 cm), so that the simulated and measured values are both areal emissions. The betaine models, whose TMA excretion was mostly set by the uptake bound rather than by biomass, were converted with the volume-weighted DNA concentration of each core. Pearson (R^2^) and Spearman (ρ, with exact permutation p values) correlations were calculated between the simulated and measured emissions of the six unrestored cores, and linear equations of the line-of-best-fit were reported.
edits.rationale: The stored fluxes were simulated with each model's biomass fixed to the mean over depths of relative abundance divided by DNA. Two depths have almost no DNA (R2_B_D1 and R2_C_D2, 0.16 µg g−1 soil), so that input carries a 1/DNA term, which multiplying by the core's DNA does not cancel. Both the draft's fits (R² 0.978/0.968/0.862, both axes divided by DNA) and an intermediate 'areal' correction (ρ = 0.60) came from that term: the factor VW_DNA × mean(1/DNA) alone has ρ = 0.60 against measured methane. On the consistent basis used here, each MAG's flux per unit of simulated abundance (a constant for every MePn model) is rescaled to its biomass in the core (relative abundance × DNA × layer thickness).
edits.sources: clauded_insights/modelling_consistent_basis_r232.json (modelling_consistent_basis_r232.py)

edits.old: Soil DNA density was significantly positively correlated with methane flux (Figure S7), therefore, we only used methane emissions and fluxes that were normalized by DNA density for all modeling efforts.
edits.new: Soil DNA concentration was weakly and not significantly correlated with methane flux (Figure S7; R^2^ = 0.22, Spearman ρ = 0.52, p = 0.08, n = 12 cores). The models were scaled by relative abundances normalized by DNA concentration, and for comparison with the measured emissions the simulated fluxes were converted to areal emissions from each member’s biomass in each core (Methods).
edits.rationale: Figure S7's own fit (y = 256.82x + 116.18) has R² = 0.22; Pearson p = 0.12; Spearman ρ = 0.52, p = 0.08; n = 12.
edits.sources: clauded_insights/modelling_consistent_basis_r232.json (modelling_consistent_basis_r232.py)

edits.new: With a phosphate source ratio of 0.07 (at least 0.07 mol of methylphosphonate per mol of inorganic phosphate, about 6.5% of the phosphate taken up), the simulated methane production of the 38 MPn-consumer models amounted to 14% of the experimental methane emissions in total and did not track their differences among the six unrestored cores (Figure 7; Spearman ρ = 0.03, exact p = 1.0, n = 6; R^2^ = 0.02).
edits.rationale: consistent areal basis, 2026 models

Betaine-model caveats: the betaine reductase reaction rxn17220_c0 is added by hand (as in the original protocol) and carries the RAST betaine-reductase genes as its gene rule, because the templates have no complex for those roles; the models are aerobic (no betaine model grows without O2), so an anaerobic enzyme is simulated in aerobic models; TMA has no unique optimum in 43 of the 108 model×core cells (with every value at its FVA minimum or maximum, the total is 2.5- or 4.5-fold the measured emissions). edits.old: Figure 7. Assessing methylphosphonate and betaine metabolism
edits.new: Figure 7. Simulated versus measured methane emissions in the six unrestored cores. Orange: summed methane flux of the methylphosphonate-consuming models (38 of the 39 MPn-consumer species; JASFMS01.1 did not grow), each model's methane per unit of simulated biomass rescaled to its biomass in the core (relative abundance × soil DNA concentration of each depth, weighted by depth); filled circles at a phosphate source ratio of 0.07 and open circles at 0.33. One *Roseovarius* model (Roseovarius.2) releases no methane at 0.07 because its annotated methane monooxygenase oxidizes it. Blue: summed methane of the 18 betaine-reducing models (methane = 0.06 × TMA excretion), converted with the core’s volume-weighted DNA concentration because their TMA excretion is partly set by the uptake bound. Both axes are in µmol CH~4~ m^−2^ d^−1^ on log scales; the dotted line marks 1:1 agreement and the dashed lines are linear fits (methylphosphonate models at 0.07, and betaine models). Methylphosphonate-derived methane is 14% of the measured emissions in total at 0.07 (5–33% among cores; 55% at 0.33) and does not track them (Spearman ρ = 0.03; R^2^ = 0.02); betaine-derived methane exceeds them in every core (1.6- to 5.5-fold) and is not significantly correlated with them (ρ = 0.60, exact p = 0.24; R^2^ = 0.08). Guild abundance versus methane is shown in Figure 9 and Table 5.

edits.old: The MAG-derived models were subjected
edits.new: 2026 models (added 2026-11-23; reassembly_2026/modelling_2026/models/README.md). Built on TF with ModelSEEDpy (fork sync-cshenry-main 311f720) and the curated templates of modelling_2026/templates/; arm A (RAST) won the pre-registered annotation comparison (annotation_comparison/RESULTS.md). Decisions for the authors: (1) JASFMS01.1 was dropped because it cannot make ribose-5-phosphate; one reaction (sedoheptulose-1,7-bisphosphatase, rxn01345) rescues it but fails two ATP tests. (2) The methanogen model (Methanolobus.1) grows as a methyl-to-acetate acetogen without making methane, so it was not simulated; the manuscript's 'dimethylamine and hydrogen' medium has no surviving code (the model grows on it, 1.32 h−1, but makes methane only apart from growth). (3) Roseovarius.2 carries a RAST methane monooxygenase (rxn00844) that oxidizes its MePn methane at the lactate optimum; closing it gives 15% instead of 14% of the measured methane at 0.07. (4) Template curation queue: betaine reductase rxn11678 and glycine reductase rxn11676 are written in the synthesis direction; Fpo rxn24614 is '<' only; four N-cycle reactions are reversible; the betaine reductase roles have no complex. The earlier repair of three MePn-obligate 2020 models does not apply: no 2026 model needs MePn.

edits.old: Metabolic models were developed using dereplicated medium and high quality
edits.new: Metabolic models were built for the representative MAG of each MPn-consumer and betaine-reducer species of the re-assembled MAG set (39 and 18 species; Table 4), one model per species and guild. Prodigal genes were annotated with the RAST service (53), and draft models were built with ModelSEEDpy, which implements the KBase modeling pipeline (52), from the current ModelSEED templates with our curations (Gram-negative v7, Gram-positive v7 and Archaea v6 templates for 31, 19 and 6 models, respectively). RAST alone was chosen over drafts that also used KOfam, eggNOG-mapper v2.1.13 and Bakta v1.12.0 annotations by criteria fixed in advance (gene-associated and gapfilled reactions, guild-pathway support, ATP production without a carbon source, and the fraction of blocked reactions): the added annotations raised the number of gene-associated reactions, but they also raised the fraction of blocked reactions by 2.7–6.5 percentage points, beyond the pre-set limit of 2, and the two that included eggNOG-mapper let one model make ATP from ammonia and oxygen. ATP production was corrected on 54 test media, and the models were gapfilled as in the original protocol: MPn consumers first on aerobic lactate with phosphate and then on lactate with MPn as the only phosphorus source, after a C–P lyase pathway and an MPn transporter were added where absent; betaine reducers on aerobic lactate, after which betaine reductase, glycine reductase and TMA export were added. Reactions that let a model oxidize ammonia (reversed nitrite and hydroxylamine reductases) or consume methane without annotation support were restricted to their reductive or methane-producing directions, and models that lost growth were gapfilled again. One MPn-consumer model (JASFMS01.1) could not grow and was excluded, leaving 38 MPn-consumer and 18 betaine-reducer models; none of the MPn-consumer models required MPn to grow.
edits.rationale: Methods for the 2026 models (models/README.md, annotation_comparison/RESULTS.md). The draft's KBase MS2 build of the 2020 MAGs and the methanogen medium sentence no longer apply: the methanogen model is not simulated (comment on P36).

Aerobic L-lactate remains the cheapest medium for the MePn consumers, but for the betaine reducers it ranks 16 of 22 (anaerobic pyruvate and fumarate need none), and no betaine model grows without O2 although these organisms (Bacillota such as Halanaerobium, M55B127) are anaerobic Stickland fermenters.
